chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The father is not killed for his son if he killed him, and the son is killed for his father if he killed his father.

key_terms.يُقْتَلُ: He is killed/executed (for blood money or retribution)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on executing a father for killing his son in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the principle of individual liability in qisas, distinguishing between paternal and filial homicide to prevent collective family retribution. While the father is exempt from execution for killing his son due to his authority (tadbir), the son is executed for killing his father, reflecting the hierarchical structure of the family in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the balance between justice and the preservation of familial bonds, a key theme in Usul al-Kafi.
